issues.quote: It is my father's silver watch. He died in 1889, and I have never let anyone regulate it, not even Uncle Aurèle. It has always been troublesome.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives only one comparison: at the nine o'clock bell the watch showed twenty minutes to nine. It says nothing about the watch's error being constant, drifting, or erratic over the evening.
issues.misreading: A solver could take 'always been troublesome' as a steady, known error and apply a fixed correction to every 'by my watch' reading (10:15, 10:18, 10:21, 10:32). Or they could conclude the watch is unreliable in general and discount all of its readings. Either reading changes the clock times the puzzle depends on, and the sheet supports neither.

issues.quote: The library ceiling is his pine floor.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that the thump was on the floor 'right above me, in the atelier.' It does not say whose floor or workshop the atelier is.
issues.misreading: 'His' could be read as Girard's or the uncle's, and the solver could take the atelier to belong to one particular man. That is an ownership claim the sheet does not make.
